items.title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
items.summary: System One models such as Jev return decisions through fast, parallel prediction. In this paper, we introduce Jeveration, showing that the same decision paradigm can also generate high-quality images in a single forward pass. items.title: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive
items.summary: Streaming video LLMs can continuously observe the world, yet often handle user requests in isolation. We introduce ALIVE, an interactive streaming video model supporting proactive monitoring, streaming task coordination, and feedback-seeking interaction. items.title: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling
items.summary: High-resolution weather prediction is important for resolving local atmospheric patterns missed by coarse global forecasts. Large pretrained weather backbones have improved global forecasting, but adapting them to produce future high-resolution fields from recent coarse states remains challenging and costly. items.title: Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development
items.summary: Games are a rich testbed for visual agents, demanding perception, long-horizon planning, and precise control. However, collecting human gameplay is costly, and learning from gameplay videos requires inferring missing actions. Existing datasets also cover a limited range of games, often without explicit tasks or verifiable outcomes. items.title: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
items.summary: A central challenge in adapting large language models (LLMs) is capability preservation: an adaptation can achieve its target while degrading general capabilities. items.summary: World action models (WAMs) have shown promising generalization and data efficiency in robot manipulation by coupling action generation with predictions of future visual dynamics. items.summary: Multimodal tabular learning involves classification and regression on tables combining structured numerical and categorical features with unstructured text and images. items.summary: Rules govern how player actions change interactive worlds. Different rules create distinct gameplay experiences within similar scenes and action spaces. items.summary: Interactive video world models turn user commands into the exploration of a generated scene, which requires the scene to keep its 3D structure as the camera moves and each action to keep a stable effect. items.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
items.summary: Post-training quantization is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost. However, the best quantization recipe differs across models and precisions. items.title: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: Latent diffusion models rely on a decoder to map denoised latents to pixels, adding complexity and inference cost. items.title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Video rough-cut is a core stage in media production workflows, organizing raw media materials into an initial video cut. Despite recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) for video-related tasks, automatic rough-cut remains underexplored, without a comprehensive benchmark for evaluation or mature workflows for producing executable cut plans. items.title: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards
items.summary: Personalized vision-language assistants use visual observations and personal memories to provide advice tailored to the user. items.summary: NPU design-space exploration for LLM inference mainly relies on an expensive simulator that often returns only scalar feedback such as latency and power. items.summary: Large language models have reduced the effort to generate code for interactive software with graphical user interfaces (GUIs). items.summary: We present Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B to 27B) that coevolves model capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI). items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are rapidly becoming a dominant paradigm for AI applications. items.title: BLIP-Live: Balancing Timeliness & Firing Precision in Proactive Streaming Video Agents
items.summary: Streaming video understanding is becoming increasingly important for real-world interactive systems. Such systems must be proactive for natural and useful human interaction: they should respond as soon as sufficient evidence becomes available while avoiding premature, redundant, or incorrect responses.
